content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model is overly conservative, often missing upward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns positive after a dip, model fails to react quickly — delay in upward price adjustment.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to premature retracement in forecast.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 7 days.
- Spike recovery: after a price spike, model underestimates the rebound — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for recovery phase.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.1, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% to account for overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.3, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to capture hidden momentum.
